uk_unfair_dismissal.description: Advise whether an employee has a viable ordinary unfair-dismissal claim under the Employment Rights Act 1996 (eligibility, fairness, time limit, compensation).

steps.question: Has the employee been dismissed by the employer within the statutory meaning of section 95 (taking into account the effective date of termination under section 97)?

Does the employee satisfy the continuous employment qualifying period required under section 108 (normally two years), including any statutory extension of the effective date of termination under section 97 read with section 86?

Was the reason, or the principal reason, for the dismissal one that makes it automatically unfair under section 99 (pregnancy, childbirth, maternity and other family reasons), section 100 (health and safety) or section 103A (protected disclosure), so that section 108(3) disapplies the two-year qualifying period?

Has the tribunal complaint been presented—or can it still be presented—within three months of the effective date of termination under section 111 (subject to statutory extensions or reasonable practicability)?

Is the dismissal unfair under section 98, because the employer cannot demonstrate a potentially fair statutory reason or because the employer acted unreasonably in treating that reason as sufficient to dismiss?
Is the employee entitled to a compensatory award under section 123, subject to the applicable statutory cap and calculation rules under section 124?

start_date.note: The date on which the employee began their period of continuous employment. Pitfall: Confusing initial engagement under non-employment arrangements with the start of employment under a contract of employment.

termination_date.note: The standard date on which the employment contract ends (e.g., when notice expires, when summary dismissal takes effect, or when a limited-term contract ends). Pitfall: Conflating the contractual termination date with the statutory effective date of termination extended by section 97 for qualifying service calculations.

notice_given.note: Whether notice to terminate the contract of employment was served by the employer or the employee. Pitfall: Treating payment in lieu of notice as dismissal with notice rather than summary dismissal without notice.

notice_given_date.note: The calendar date on which notice of termination was communicated to the other party. Pitfall: Confusing the date the notice letter was drafted with the date it was actually received and took effect.

advice_date.note: The date on which legal advice is being provided. Pitfall: Failing to assess ongoing time limits under section 111 relative to this date when advising whether a prospective claim is still in time.

claim_presented_date.note: The date on which the unfair dismissal complaint is submitted to the employment tribunal. Pitfall: Assuming a claim cannot be presented before the termination date when notice has been given, contrary to section 111(3).

annual_pay.note: The employee's total annual remuneration. Pitfall: Including non-contractual or unearned benefits improperly when calculating annual pay, or failing to reconcile it with weekly pay for statutory cap calculations under section 124.

weekly_pay.note: The employee's gross weekly remuneration used to determine the 52 weeks' pay limit under section 124(1ZA). Pitfall: Miscalculating a week's pay where variable pay or bonuses are involved.

age.note: The chronological age of the claimant. Pitfall: Relying on age to establish basic eligibility for ordinary unfair dismissal, whereas continuous service under section 108 is the determinative criterion.

uk_redundancy_payment.description: Advise whether an employee is entitled to a statutory redundancy payment under the Employment Rights Act 1996, and how it is calculated.

steps.question: Has the employee been dismissed by the employer within the statutory definition under section 136?

Is the dismissal wholly or mainly attributable to the employer ceasing or intending to cease business (either entirely or where the employee worked) or to diminished requirements for employees to carry out work of a particular kind?

Does the employee keep the right to a redundancy payment under section 141? Answer yes if no offer to renew the contract or to re-engage the employee was made, or the offered employment was not suitable, or the employee refused it reasonably. Answer no if the employee unreasonably refused an offer to which section 141 applies.
Has the statutory relevant date of dismissal been determined, incorporating any extension required by section 86 statutory minimum notice?
Did the employee have at least two years of continuous employment ending with the relevant date?
Has the redundancy payment been calculated in accordance with the statutory rules by reckoning backwards up to 20 years of service and applying the weekly pay cap?

start_date.note: The date on which the employee's continuous period of employment began; critical for calculating continuous service under section 155 and section 162.

termination_date.note: The date on which employment terminates; must be distinguished from the statutory relevant date where section 145(5) applies statutory minimum notice extensions.

notice_given.note: Whether statutory or contractual notice of termination was given by the employer or the employee; determines which subsection of section 145 defines the relevant date.

notice_given_date.note: The date notice was communicated; required to determine the obligatory notice period, counter-notice validity under section 136(3), and minimum notice compliance under section 86.

advice_date.note: The date of assessing liability and advising the client, used as the benchmark date to evaluate whether requirements have been met.

claim_presented_date.note: The date any claim was brought before an employment tribunal regarding redundancy payment liability under section 162.

annual_pay.note: The employee's total annual gross earnings; used to calculate the figure for a week's pay before applying statutory caps.

weekly_pay.note: The employee's gross pay for a week; must be capped at £751 pursuant to section 227 when calculating the statutory redundancy payment.

age.note: The employee's age during each reckoned year of continuous service; determines the multiple of a week's pay allocated under section 162 when counting backwards from the relevant date.
